what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 4: Attraction without growth: bodies that slow records without keeping them. SETTING (blocks 48, 49, 51, 52; open PRs 'ail48: free capturing bodies are carried by the wind', 'ail49: the attraction is tied to growth', 'ail51: the wind of a capturing body is not isotropic', 'ail52: a streaming clause with an isotropic second-order term'): inertial record gas, sphere menu (contents are unit vectors; a record of content s hops to x + sign(s_k) e_k at the rate |s_k|/sqrt 3). ESTABLISHED: with contents of unit length the only thing a body can take from the gas is records; a body whose emissions equal its captures sends no number flux through any surface around it and draws no inverse-square wind (block 49, exact), so the attraction of capturing bodies is tied to their growth, q_1 = (8 pi/3)(1 - rho) G. For independent records (no exchange, no scattering) the deficit behind a capturing site is the multinomial hitting probability h(x, s) of the directed walk with step frequencies |s_k|/|s|_1, its integral over the simplex of step frequencies is 1/((n+1)(n+2)) at every site of the shell n = |x|_1, and the force on a transparent capturing site is (rho/(4 pi sqrt 3)) m |r|_1^2/r^2 (m = 1, 2, 4 off the coordinate planes, on a plane, on an axis), with large 1/r corrections (block 48). NOT WORKED, and the subject of this problem: the classical shadow picture takes SPEED from its corpuscles, not the corpuscles themselves. TASK: extend the menu: a content is a vector v = m s with direction s (unit) and magnitude m in (0, 1]; a record hops to x + sign(s_k) e_k at the rate m |s_k|/sqrt 3. A SLOWING site lets a record pass and multiplies its content by kappa in (0, 1): it takes the momentum (1 - kappa) v and keeps no record. (a) For independent records and one slowing site at the origin, find the stationary densities of slowed and unslowed records of each content at every site (the number flux through every site is unchanged; the slowed records are denser by 1/kappa), using block 48's hitting probability h(x, s). (b) Compute the momentum taken per tick by a second slowing site at x: show that the isotropic part cancels and that the net push is towards the first site, equal to (1 - kappa_1)(1 - kappa_2) times block 48's collisionless force with the weight <m^2> of the magnitudes; say whether action and reaction are equal, and confirm that neither body grows. (c) The price: compute the rate at which the gas loses speed to a population of slowing sites of density n_b, and compare it with the pull per pair: the pull goes as (1 - kappa)^2 and the run-down as (1 - kappa); state the inequality that a gas which has not run down after T ticks imposes on the pull. (d) With scattering that re-draws a pair of contents on its momentum class (magnitudes included): show that the slowed beam heals within about a mean free path and say how the force is screened at distances beyond it. (e) State plainly what the mechanism adds to the axioms (a menu with magnitudes; a slowing clause) and whether it survives block 51's direction dependence (it lives without collisions, where the force has the coefficient |r|_1^2) or block 52's biased walk. check.py: exact rational verification of (a) and (b) on a small block for rational contents, in the manner of block 48's runner (scripts/admissibility_rule_free_capturing_bodies_*.py on its PR branch).  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/bodies-that-slow-records-without-keeping-them/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/bodies-that-slow-records-without-keeping-them/<name>/check.py"
